doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Billie at the Harmony Inn with Mealy
summary: After Rodgers she worked at the Harmony Inn with Mealy, Lawrence Toca and a drummer for about a year.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: October the seventh, 1959. Oh, that's right. Let's see. So, Billy, where did we leave off with you? We might as well finish you off. May have to come back for DD some more later. We got you back for lunch, isn't it? Yeah, I got back for lunch.
Yeah, and you left the job with Rogers, and then what happened?
Mm-hmm. And what happened? And what happened?
I went to stuff with stuff with I went to work again, I went to work at the hominine I made, at Mealy Nell. The hominine? Yeah, at Mealy Nell. The hominine. Yeah. And the hominine.
Mealy Barnes on clarinet, huh? Yeah. And Claybear? No. No, uh. What you saying?
Who was on drums? Joey Channaboy?
No, Joey Channaboy. No.
Who was on drums? Who was on drums? What did I say?
I believe it.
Lawrence on trumpet.
Lawrence.
What was that?
What was that?

What was that? Lawrence. No, Mealy and Mealy worked together down there. Lawrence and Mealy was working there for us, they got really defied Lawrence. And, uh, Mealy and Lawrence, and, uh, Gilly, what did he make the drummer name? Gilly. Mealy was Gilly. I believe it was Gilly on drums. Well, that's enough.
Gilly ain't gonna find his name. I believe it was Gilly on drums. Mm-hmm.
And how long were you down there at the Harmonian? Oh, I was at the Harmonian? I guess pretty near about a year, anyway. Mm-hmm. And then what? The Man Fighters.
The Man Fighters, huh?
Well, they put a white band in there, he'll be the best. It was Mealy Jar, but, man, he wasn't in my way, it was Mealy Jar. I went and worked with Mealy down there and put a hitbitter band in there.
Well, they got on the host, I mean, he managed on the host.
And then where did you go to?
Let me see where did I go to then? Let me see. Well I don't know no where I saw with you, cause I stayed with old folks so long down there.
